scenarioStory.history: Patient was swimming with friends at a public lake and went underwater; friends estimate approximately 5 minutes before he was located and pulled to the dock by a lifeguard. The lifeguard began rescue breathing immediately. No reported diving, no witnessed trauma, water temperature moderate (not near-freezing).
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find an 18-year-old male supine on the dock, apneic, with a weak carotid pulse. Skin is cold, wet, and cyanotic. Lifeguard has been providing rescue breaths. → BVM with PEEP started: Crew ventilates with BVM and PEEP at an adult apnea rate, monitoring oxygenation closely and avoiding hyperoxygenation per the drowning guideline. → Rewarming and warmed IV fluids started: Crew removes wet clothing, insulates the patient, applies field rewarming with heat packs wrapped in a barrier, and establishes IV access for a warmed crystalloid bolus while continuing ventilatory support. → Ventilation and rewarming improving, transport initiated: Spontaneous respiratory effort is returning, perfusion is improving, and the patient is transported to a hospital capable of rewarming and resuscitation with the ambulance compartment warmed.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Pulled unresponsive from lake water, apneic

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find an 18-year-old male supine on the dock, apneic, with a weak carotid pulse. Skin is cold, wet, and cyanotic. Lifeguard has been providing rescue breaths.
relatedChecklist: Begin BVM ventilation with PEEP 5 cmH2O at 1 breath every 6 seconds (10/min) for apnea
Titrate oxygen/PEEP to target SpO2 94–98%; avoid hyperoxygenation

scenarioEvents.name: BVM with PEEP started
scenarioEvents.description: Crew ventilates with BVM and PEEP at an adult apnea rate, monitoring oxygenation closely and avoiding hyperoxygenation per the drowning guideline.
relatedChecklist: Remove wet clothing, dry skin, insulate with dry blankets and a vapor barrier
Apply heat packs to torso wrapped in a barrier; never place directly on skin
Establish IV access; give warmed isotonic crystalloid bolus, repeat as needed

scenarioEvents.name: Rewarming and warmed IV fluids started
scenarioEvents.description: Crew removes wet clothing, insulates the patient, applies field rewarming with heat packs wrapped in a barrier, and establishes IV access for a warmed crystalloid bolus while continuing ventilatory support.
relatedChecklist: Transport to hospital capable of rewarming/resuscitation; warm ambulance to at least 24°C

scenarioEvents.name: Ventilation and rewarming improving, transport initiated
scenarioEvents.description: Spontaneous respiratory effort is returning, perfusion is improving, and the patient is transported to a hospital capable of rewarming and resuscitation with the ambulance compartment warmed.

scenarioEvents.name: Ventilation delayed, pulse lost
scenarioEvents.description: BVM ventilation is delayed or ineffective while the patient remains apneic and hypothermic. The pulse is lost and the patient progresses into cardiac arrest, requiring the drowning-specific ABC approach rather than standard compressions-first CPR.
relatedChecklist: Recognize drowning-specific arrest; give 5 rescue breaths, then continue 30:2 CPR

scenarioEvents.name: Heat pack applied without barrier
scenarioEvents.description: A heat pack is placed directly against bare skin without a barrier during field rewarming. A thermal burn injury develops at the contact site, compounding patient morbidity in a patient with reduced ability to sense or report the injury.
relatedChecklist: Recognize thermal injury; remove direct heat source and place a barrier before reapplying
